1.why: Text uses a clean sans-serif face at reasonable size with comfortable line spacing and clear headings, though monospace code blocks and log panels are tighter.

2.why: No italics or all-caps body text (only the small 'NORTHSTAR BANK' wordmark) and paragraphs are one or two short lines, so dense text blocks are avoided apart from the dark log dumps.

3.why: The layout is a single narrow centred column that would scale to a phone, but nothing in the screenshots is shown at mobile width and the long wrapped otpauth:// string and log panel would be cramped.

4.why: Each screen has a one-sentence instruction in plain language, e.g. 'Store these recovery codes somewhere secure. Each code works once.'

5.why: Only the recovery code field shows a format example placeholder (ABCD-EFGH-JKLM); the verification code and authenticator code fields show no example of expected input.

6.why: Progression never requires reading more than a couple of short sentences; the longest content (secret/otpauth string and logs) is optional reference material.

7.why: No copy button or copy affordance is present anywhere — the manual secret, otpauth URI and eight recovery codes are plain read-only text that must be transcribed.

8.why: No QR code is rendered; only a raw 'Provisioning representation' otpauth:// text string is offered, which cannot be scanned.

9.why: Standard login name/password inputs exist and could attract autofill, but there is no visible evidence of autocomplete attributes or one-time-code support and code fields are generic.

10.why: The primary green button is visually prominent, but there is no step indicator or progress marker showing which stage of enrolment the user is at.

11.why: Most screens ask one thing, but step 4 presents secret display, code entry and 'Enable MFA and show recovery codes' at once, and the recovery screen offers two competing buttons.

12.why: Some outcomes are stated ('MFA is enabled'), but there is no confirmation after identity verification and no statement of what comes next after storing recovery codes.

13.why: The user can re-request codes via 'Generate replacement recovery codes' and retry sign-in repeatedly, but there is no reveal/hide toggle and no option to re-send the verification code.

14.why: Errors are unhelpful and technical: a raw JavaScript exception ('Failed to execute insertBefore on Node...') and repeated 'Unable to continue sign-in.' with no cause or fix, stacking up to eight times.

15.why: No visible countdown timer is imposed on reading, but the page states codes rotate every 30 seconds and verification codes are 'short-lived', so entry time is not generous.
